core_assessment:
Read every selected statement and proof block 196-454,455-1231,1233-1746,1748-2165,2167-2513,2515-2617 before consulting the selector difficulty_reason. The shifted dual convention and cone compatibility determine the pairing degree. The two finite-flat devissages distinguish the locally compact H1 contribution from the finite other local groups; compact-support localization gives the strict topology and the profinite conclusion, subject to the finite/profinite wording correction recorded below.
The torus and character-lattice finite-type statements are proved from units, finite class groups, Hochschild-Serre, Kummer and cohomological dimension. The class E argument identifies low-degree local and compact-support groups as a product of a profinite and a finitely generated discrete group. This supplies injectivity into arithmetic completion and agreement with the completion by open finite-index subgroups exactly where the end of the proof needs it.
Finite-flat AMM duality is extended to complexes by the retained five-lemma devissage. For C tensor Z/n, the dual shift is explicit and produces the two differently oriented finite/profinite pairings. The ell-primary argument controls kernels by duals of torsion-free Tate modules; it does not assume the characteristic-p groups finite. In particular, the exclusions i=-1,0 in the second direct-limit argument at1647 and1737-1741 are necessary and respected. The later low-degree completed pairings use the separate Kummer diagrams and class E completion instead of the invalid shortcut.
D-group duality is used only for a proper open U, as required by the finite-group inputs. Shrinking U yields surjections of finite D groups; stabilization then identifies them with the everywhere locally trivial Sha groups. For Sha0/Sha2, the additional injectivity lemma first kills the finite kernels of H1(U,T)->H1(K,T), then dualizes injections between completions of finitely generated H0 groups to obtain the compact-support surjections needed for stabilization.
For ptstart, inverse limits of the finite-place sequences remain exact because the kernels inside D0(U,C) are finite (and vanish in degree -1); the later kernels of s_V have surjective transition maps since they are images of the same H^i(U,hat C). The discrete-image lemma uses finite intersection with an open unramified subgroup in the lattice/higher-degree cases and the retained closed-image lemma in degrees -1,0. Thus the images used in the final dualization are strict, not merely algebraically injective.
The high-degree rows follow by compact-support localization and direct limits, with the correct refin1 pairing. The two completed low-degree fragments follow by dualizing the strict sequence for the discrete global image and applying local unramified annihilators plus finite Sha duality. The arithmetic completion is needed at exactly the two exceptions printed in the theorem. The number-field remarks2105-2165 neither supply hypotheses nor extend the counted statement.

All passage from these one-group facts to complexes, all completion arguments, and every global duality conclusion remain required author-proof work. The elementary topological fact that a strict extension of profinite Hausdorff groups is profinite is the precise fact used to interpret451; no new arithmetic lemma is needed.

issues.explanation: The quotient used to topologize Hc^i is the local degree(i-1) quotient in the printed sequence405, whereas435 prints degree i. At431 the right group should carry the generic degree i of427-428. More substantially,451 cannot generally call the outer group finite/discrete: Hc^2(U,mu_p) may be infinite, as the same author explicitly notes at1578. The already specified strict devissage expresses the middle group as an extension of closed-subgroup/quotient profinite terms by induction; a strict Hausdorff extension of profinite groups is profinite. Indeed quotient by a compact kernel is a closed map with compact fibers, so compactness lifts from the quotient, and connected components map trivially into the totally disconnected quotient and then lie trivially in the kernel. This uses the author devissage unchanged and only the weaker profinite premise that its own induction provides. Do not reproduce the stronger finite assertion as a proved fact.
